briefdescription.para: Number types and primitive operations for forward-mode automatic differentiation.

detaileddescription.para:
All Marmot code uses the types and functions declared here instead of naming the implementations directly:
Hyper-dual and Taylor numbers (dual, dual2nd, dual3rd, HyperDual, Taylor): ScalarMode (MarmotAutomaticDifferentiationScalarMode.h).
JacobianDual, the number type of the first-derivative drivers (df_dT, dF_dT, fixed-size dF_dX): VectorMode::Dual (MarmotAutomaticDifferentiationVectorMode.h), which computes all directions in a single evaluation.
HessianDual, the number type of the second-derivative driver d2f_dT2: VectorMode::Dual2nd (MarmotAutomaticDifferentiationVectorModeSecondOrder.h), which computes the gradient and the Hessian in a single evaluation.

Vocabulary:
HyperDual<order>: nested dual number with one independent direction per nesting level; level 1 is the outermost level. dual, dual2nd and dual3rd are the orders 1, 2 and 3.
Taylor<order>: univariate truncated Taylor number carrying the derivatives 0..order of one variable.
JacobianDual<nDirections>: number type of the first-derivative drivers df_dT, dF_dT and dF_dX< n >, with nDirections independent variables. Code differentiated by these drivers must use this type, not dual.
seed<level>( x, v ) sets the derivative of x along nesting level level to v, derivative<level>( y ) reads the mixed derivative of y along the levels 1..level, value( y ) reads the primal value.
HessianDual<nDirections>: number type of the second-derivative driver d2f_dT2, with nDirections independent variables. Code differentiated by d2f_dT2 must use this type, not dual2nd.
For vector-mode numbers (isVectorDual, isHessianDual), seedDirection( x, i ) makes x the independent variable i and partialDerivative( y, i ) reads the partial derivative of y with respect to variable i; secondPartialDerivative( y, i, j ) reads a second partial derivative of a HessianDual.
